title: Orsen and the Promise
premise: Emrys Halloran, a wedding planner who swore off love after his own engagement collapsed, is hired to orchestrate a high-profile society wedding — only to discover the bride and groom are two rivals from his past, stranded together years ago by a snowstorm with a secret that ruined all three of them. As he plans their impossible union, old wounds reopen and Emrys must choose between protecting his carefully rebuilt life and telling the truth that could free them all. When the bakery lease below his office — his last tie to stability — runs out on the eve of the ceremony, Emrys finally forgives himself for the mistake of his twenties, exposes the corruption threatening the couple's families, and chooses a future built not on safety but on honest, imperfect love.
about_author: Tamsin Voss is a former event coordinator who spent a decade behind the scenes of other people's happily-ever-afters before turning to fiction. She writes stories about people who rebuild themselves out of wreckage, and she still cries at weddings — professionally.

chapters.title: The Measure of Small Steps
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Five years after his broken engagement, Emrys runs a meticulous wedding planning business above a bakery whose lease is quietly expiring. A routine consultation shows how tightly he controls every detail of love except his own. Emotional beat: brittle competence masking grief.

chapters.title: The Halloran Clause
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A lucrative contract arrives: plan the wedding of socialite Vivienne Ashe to tech magnate Callum Reyes. Emrys recognizes both names — the snowstorm, the mistake, the fallout that ended his engagement. He almost refuses; the fee would save the bakery lease. Beat: temptation versus self-protection.

chapters.title: Two Rivals, One Ballroom
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. Vivienne and Callum negotiate their merger-marriage like a hostile acquisition, all cold terms and colder glances. Vivienne privately wonders why Emrys flinched at her name. Beat: unease beneath the gilded surface.

chapters.title: What the Snow Kept
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Flashback woven through present: the mountain lodge, the storm, the promise three twenty-somethings made and broke. Callum believes Emrys betrayed them first. Beat: resentment sharpened by longing for what they lost.

chapters.title: Tasting Menu, Bitter Finish
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. First joint planning session detonates when an old photograph surfaces in Vivienne's mood board. Emrys deflects with professionalism while his hands shake. The baker, Nell, offers him a lease extension contingent on pulling off this wedding flawlessly. Beat: pressure mounting from every side.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. Vivienne corners Emrys alone; she knows more about the snowstorm than she's admitted. She proposes a truce: her silence about his past in exchange for making this wedding work. Beat: uneasy alliance, mutual leverage.

chapters.title: The Guest List Is a Weapon
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum's father pressures him to use the wedding to bury a business scandal, inviting guests who can whitewash it. Callum realizes his marriage is becoming collateral. Beat: power's quiet corruption taking root.

chapters.title: Nell's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Late night with Nell over failed cake tastings; she shares how she rebuilt after losing her own family, planting the novel's found-family thread. Emrys admits, for the first time aloud, that he blames himself for the snowstorm. Beat: first crack in his armor.

chapters.title: Rehearsal of Lies
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. The rehearsal dinner forces the trio into one room. Old chemistry flickers dangerously between all three; a toast goes wrong and nearly exposes everything. Beat: desire and dread entwined.

chapters.title: Lease Expiry
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The landlord serves formal notice: the bakery building will be sold unless the wedding's success secures Nell's tenancy clause. Emrys understands the wedding has become his cage. Beat: stakes made concrete and personal.

chapters.title: The Second Storm
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. A freak early blizzard strands the wedding party at the same mountain lodge — history repeating. Trapped together, the trio can no longer perform civility. Beat: claustrophobic rising tension.

chapters.title: Confessions at Altitude
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. By firelight, the truth of the snowstorm finally spills: each believed the others abandoned them; each carried a private guilt. Vivienne confesses she orchestrated the reunion deliberately. Beat: betrayal inside revelation.

chapters.title: What Emrys Did
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys admits his own sin — he left that night to protect his engagement, choosing respectability over the two people who loved him, then let them take the blame. Beat: the person in the mirror, finally faced.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum walks into the storm rather than forgive. Vivienne follows; Emrys organizes the search, discovering along the way evidence of Callum's father's sabotage of the company — and the wedding. Beat: external danger mirroring internal rupture.

chapters.title: Found
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys finds Callum half-frozen and talks him back, saying the words he never said five years ago. They return to find Vivienne has called his father out before the trapped guests. Beat: catharsis through rescue and truth-telling.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Back in the city, Callum confronts his father, risking his inheritance and name to expose the scandal. He loses the company but keeps his integrity — and asks Emrys and Vivienne, not shareholders, what comes next. Beat: power renounced, self reclaimed.

chapters.title: A Wedding Nobody Planned
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. With the original spectacle dead, Vivienne tears up the contract and asks Emrys to plan something true instead — small, imperfect, real. Emrys hesitates: he still doesn't believe in weddings. Beat: invitation to faith.

chapters.title: Forgiving the Mirror
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys visits his ex-fiancé, returns the ring he kept as penance, and forgives himself at last. He signs papers surrendering his stake in the venue deal so Nell's bakery survives regardless of him. Beat: grace, chosen freely.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Guests and a Storm Door
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The small wedding comes together in the bakery itself — mismatched chairs, Nell's cakes, found family filling the room. The sky threatens snow again; everyone holds their breath. Beat: tender anticipation.

chapters.title: The Promise, Kept Differently
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. During the vows, the three rewrite the broken promise from the lodge — not possession, but presence. Snow falls harmlessly outside. Vivienne realizes love isn't the merger she planned but the family in the room. Beat: emotional climax resolved.

chapters.title: Above the Bakery
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Epilogue-adjacent: months later, Callum lives in the flat above the bakery; the three run a modest events studio together. Callum reflects on what he lost and what survived. Beat: quiet contentment earned.

chapters.title: Orsen and the Promise
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Final chapter: Emrys plans a stranger's wedding with joy instead of armor, Nell's lease renewed, his name on nothing but the door he chose. He believes in weddings again — not as promises of permanence, but as acts of courage. Beat: full-circle resolution.
